markdown_report:
The best first step is an architecture-aware, paired history-sensitivity diagnostic adapter. At 0% progress, reliable measurements provide a practical foundation for subsequent SASRec changes.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Existing margins measure sampled training separation. They cannot establish validation ranking quality. (2) Mean embedding cosine measures directional alignment. It cannot independently establish collapse or personalization. (3) Qualitative feedback suggests insufficient specificity and possible stale-history influence. These are hypotheses, because present intent, ownership and compatibility are generally unobserved.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Oh and Cho [1] motivate measuring recency dependence. Their results do not justify automatically increasing recent-item weight. (2) Liu et al. [2] identify availability confounding in shuffled histories. Order sensitivity therefore needs constrained perturbations and explicit limitations. (3) Krichene and Rendle [3] show sampled ranking can disagree with full-catalog ranking. The pinned macro validation HR@10 must remain the selection criterion.

**Directions and framework.** Organize diagnosis along three axes: representation behavior, ranking sensitivity, and evidence quality. Existing embedding probes occupy the first axis, paired perturbations connect the first two, and title/description evidence constrains interpretation. The gap is a reproducible adapter connecting measured model behavior to testable hypotheses without inventing user intent.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/implementation difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Paired history-sensitivity adapter [1,2]: 5/8/4.** Originality: useful integration, though established components. Potential: reusable across architectures, though sensitivity need not predict accuracy. Difficulty: small inference changes, though masking requires care.
- **Contextual-versus-pooled branch ablation [1,2]: 4/7/6.** Originality: interpretable comparison, though familiar. Potential: can motivate simpler models, though ablations need retraining confirmation. Difficulty: lightweight pooling, though architecture changes require a matching predictor writer.
- **Evidence-backed specificity audit: 6/6/5.** Originality: connects factual evidence to diagnosis, though the taxonomy is heuristic. Potential: clarifies qualitative failures, though intent remains unknown. Difficulty: uses available text, though reliable matching needs manual checks.

**Selected algorithm.** Cache up to ten training batches and their supplied positive/negative candidates. Compare intact sequences with equal-count recent and older deletion, repeated availability-constrained shuffling, and shuffling that preserves the final item. Preserve retained-item order during deletion and right-pad consistently with the baseline. Report paired margin changes, ranking flips, final-feature cosine distance, valid counts and perturbation coverage. Treat training results as in-sample sensitivity measurements.

```
cache batches; save model mode; enter eval/no_grad
for cached batch:
    score intact sequence on fixed candidate pairs
    construct valid seeded perturbations
    score each perturbation on the same pairs
    aggregate paired effects and eligible counts
restore model mode
return metrics, metric_definitions
```

Preserve both public diagnostic callables. Use actual model hooks, exclude padding, return null for unavailable metrics, and omit unavailable category/review probes. Interpret effects as model dependence, never causal preference. Compare subsequent interventions only through host-provided per-category and macro validation HR@10; keep splits, seeds, routing and evaluation unchanged.

idea.description: Implement a paired history-sensitivity diagnostic adapter around the actual trained model. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics with explicit definitions, counts and limitations.
idea.motivation: The current adapter measures embedding alignment and sampled training separation but does not test whether historical information affects ranking. The qualitative feedback motivates testing specificity and recency hypotheses without treating those hypotheses as observed intent.
idea.implementation_notes: Use view.model for mode management and preserve its original training state with try/finally. Cache at most ten loader batches once so every condition uses identical examples and supplied negatives. Use a local seed-42 generator without advancing training RNGs. Adapt sequence conversion to the existing log2feats contract. For B x L x D outputs, gather the final nonpadding feature using sequence masks; for candidate-pair scoring, use the matching final valid positive/negative position and verify alignment. Reject malformed outputs instead of silently broadcasting. Perturb only valid histories, retain their newest item where specified, and apply the baseline's padding convention. Choose the same deletion count for recent and older removal while retaining at least one interaction; report eligible counts. Availability-constrained shuffling requires timestamps aligned to histories and item-first-seen times computed only from public training interactions; otherwise mark that condition unavailable. Freezing candidate pairs prevents candidate sampling from changing comparisons. Report margin deltas, pairwise ordering flips, representation distance with zero-norm exclusions, seed-to-seed perturbation variation and coverage. Do not label these training diagnostics HR@10. Use null plus a reason for missing measurements; omit unavailable categories, reviews and simulator traits. The interpreter prompt must include both metrics and definitions and forbid causal intent claims. Keep DATA_DIR as os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and artifacts beneath the trial directory. This diagnostic-only intervention requires no predictor architecture change.

originality.positive: Combines architecture-aware hooks, paired ranking perturbations and explicit missing-data semantics in one reusable diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: The perturbations and representation comparisons are established techniques; the contribution is their disciplined integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides reproducible hypotheses for later pooling, recency and objective interventions across all four categories.
future_potential.negative: Sensitivity improvements may have little relationship to pinned validation HR@10 and require empirical calibration.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing inference hooks and requires no new training objective, external data or pretrained weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Padding, final-position alignment, timestamp constraints and architecture-specific score shapes require careful handling.

related_work.title: Oh and Cho (2024), recency-bias study [1]
contributions: The supplied research summary describes a recency-bias metric and performance gains from mitigating excessive recent-item emphasis.
limitations: Does not establish the appropriate recency weighting for these four datasets or validate the proposed adapter.

related_work.title: Liu et al., RecSys 2025, constrained history shuffling [2]
contributions: The supplied summary identifies item-availability confounding in random history shuffling and describes availability-respecting perturbations.
limitations: Constrained shuffling remains a model-sensitivity test; it does not identify causal user preferences.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle, On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation [3]
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can produce model comparisons that disagree with full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not replace the task's pinned sampled validation objective or establish a relationship between training sensitivity and recommendation accuracy.
